config.title: scroll-margin and scroll-padding

intro.title: scroll-margin and scroll-padding
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with multiple sections to explore how scroll-margin and scroll-padding work. You will learn how these CSS properties control the spacing around elements when they are scrolled into view, improving navigation and user experience. The core concept involves using CSS to adjust scroll behavior and prevent content from being hidden behind fixed headers. You will work with basic HTML structure and apply scroll-margin and scroll-padding in your CSS file to see their effects firsthand.
intro.usecase: The scroll-margin and scroll-padding properties are essential for creating polished, accessible navigation experiences in real-world web applications. For example, in a product documentation site with a fixed header, clicking an in-page anchor link (like a 'Jump to Section' button) can cause the target heading to appear hidden behind the header. By applying scroll-margin to the target elements or scroll-padding to the scroll container, developers ensure content scrolls into view with a clear visual offset, preventing awkward overlaps. This pattern is commonly used in dashboards with sticky navigation bars, long-form articles with a table of contents, and single-page applications with smooth scrolling sections, improving both usability and visual clarity.

Configure scroll-padding to establish consistent offset for scroll containers
Implement both scroll-margin and scroll-padding in a navigation menu with anchor links
Manipulate scroll behavior by adjusting scroll-margin values for different element positions
Initialize scroll-padding on a fixed header to prevent content from being hidden
Control scroll snapping alignment using scroll-margin on child elements
Integrate scroll-margin with CSS scroll-snap properties for smooth navigation
